summary.text: Ken Calvert is a Republican who has represented Riverside County in the U.S. House since 1992 after a career as a restaurant and real-estate small-business owner. He chairs the Defense subcommittee of the House Appropriations Committee, and Proposition 50 redistricting placed him in the same new 40th District as fellow Republican incumbent Young Kim. In the June 2 top-two primary he received 35% of the vote to Kim's 21%.

paragraphs.text: Calvert was born in Corona, California, on June 8, 1953, and describes himself as a lifelong resident of Riverside County. He graduated from Corona High School in 1971.
He attended Chaffey College, earning an associate degree in 1973 according to Ballotpedia, and then graduated from San Diego State University in 1975 with a bachelor's degree in economics.

According to his official biography, Calvert was a 17-year small-business owner in the restaurant and real estate industries, and Ballotpedia lists restaurant manager among his past jobs. Ballotpedia also says he chaired the Riverside County Republican Party.
His official biography says he has held leadership roles with local volunteer organizations including the Corona Chamber of Commerce, the Corona Rotary and the Corona-Norco Family YMCA.

Calvert was first elected to the U.S. House in 1992, defeating Democrat Mark Takano by 519 votes, 46.7% to 46.4%, according to Ballotpedia's results. His official biography describes him as one of the chamber's most senior members and the dean of the California Republican delegation.

On the House Appropriations Committee he chairs the Defense Subcommittee and also sits on the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee in the 119th Congress; Ballotpedia lists him as Defense subcommittee chair for 2023 onward.

After Proposition 50 redrew California's congressional districts in 2025, he was drawn into the 40th District with Young Kim, and the two Republican incumbents advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, with Calvert receiving 35% and Kim 21%.
